## Current benchmarks lack consistent criteria for assessing whether generated molecules have therapeutic potential

::: panel-tabset
### Metrics

```{python}
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 10
#| label: fig-lit-review-metrics
#| results: 'hide'

import os
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

# Paths for data and figures
metrics_path = 'method_processing/data/metrics.csv' 
eval_path = 'method_processing/data/evaluation.csv' 

model_cols = [
    'Gex2SGen',
    'FAME',
    'SmilesGEN',
    'GexMolGen',
    'TransGEM',
    'TRIOMPHE',
    'GxRNN',
    'BiAee',
    'BICEV',
    'Paccmann_RL'
]

# 1. Load metrics data
df_metrics = pd.read_csv(metrics_path)

# Prepare numerical data for the matrix
heatmap_data = df_metrics[model_cols].replace({r'Yes\s*': 1, r'No\s*': 0}, regex=True).fillna(0).astype(float)
heatmap_data.index = df_metrics['Metrics']

# Map 'Class' to colors for the side bars
class_palette = dict(zip(df_metrics['Class'].unique(), sns.color_palette("Set2")))

row_colors = pd.DataFrame({
    'Class': df_metrics['Class'].map(class_palette).values,
}, index=df_metrics['Metrics'])

# Create the Clustermap for Evaluated Metrics
g_metrics = sns.clustermap(
    heatmap_data,
    row_colors=row_colors,           
    cmap="Greens",                    
    linewidths=0.5, 
    cbar_pos=None,  
    linecolor='lightgray',                 
    figsize=(12, 17),
    row_cluster=False,
    col_cluster=False
)

_ = g_metrics.ax_row_colors.set_xticks([])
_ = g_metrics.ax_row_colors.set_xticklabels([])
_ = plt.setp(g_metrics.ax_heatmap.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90, horizontalalignment='center', fontsize=14)
_ = plt.setp(g_metrics.ax_heatmap.get_yticklabels(), fontsize=14)
_ = g_metrics.ax_heatmap.set_ylabel('')

# Add Legends
class_handles = [mpatches.Patch(color=color, label=label) for label, color in class_palette.items()]
yes_handle = mpatches.Patch(color=sns.color_palette("Greens")[-1], label='Yes')
no_handle = mpatches.Patch(color=sns.color_palette("Greens")[0], label='No')

class_legend = g_metrics.fig.legend(handles=class_handles, loc="upper center", frameon=False, fontsize=14)
_ = g_metrics.fig.add_artist(class_legend)

yes_no_legend = g_metrics.fig.legend(
    handles=[yes_handle, no_handle],
    title="Evaluated Metrics",
    loc="upper left",
    frameon=False,
    fontsize=14,
    title_fontsize=14,
    bbox_to_anchor=(0.88, 0.50)
)
_ = plt.show()
```

### Evaluation strategies

```{python}
#| fig-height: 12

# 2. Load evaluation strategies data

heatmap_data_eval = df_eval[model_cols].replace({r'Yes\s*': 1, r'No\s*': 0}, regex=True).fillna(0).astype(float)

}, index=df_eval['Evaluation method'])

# Create the Clustermap for Evaluation Strategies

no_handle_eval = mpatches.Patch(color=sns.color_palette("Oranges")[0], label='No')

class_legend_eval = g_eval.fig.legend(handles=class_handles_eval, loc="upper center", frameon=False, fontsize=14)

yes_no_legend_eval = g_eval.fig.legend(
    handles=[yes_handle_eval, no_handle_eval],
    title="Evaluated strategy",
    loc="upper right",
    frameon=False,
    fontsize=14,
    title_fontsize=14
)

_ = plt.show()
```

## TheraFlow provides a staged evaluation framework for transcriptomics-guided molecular generation

TheraFlow integrates more than 70 complementary evaluation metrics spanning model-level generative performance and molecule-level chemical, structural and biological properties. @fig-1 is a comparitve heatmap showing selected metrics

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 15
#| label: fig-1

df = fread("outputs/merged_master_dataframe.csv")

columns = c("SMILES", "method", "QED", "SA_Score", "MW", "LogP", "HBA", "HBD", "Passes_Safety", "Sim_Morg_Tani", "internal_energy", "internal_steric_clash", "aromatic_ring_flatness", "non-aromatic_ring_non-flatness", "number_short_outlier_bonds", "number_long_outlier_bonds", "most_extreme_relative_angle", "reversal_score_scaled")
df = df %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(columns))%>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ {
    # If the column is logical, convert to numeric before taking the mean
    if(is.logical(.x)) {
      mean(as.numeric(.x), na.rm = TRUE)
    } else if(is.numeric(.x)) {
      mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  })) %>%
  ungroup()

gen_metrics = fread("outputs/set_properties.csv") # note the change 
gen_metrics <- gen_metrics %>%
  mutate(method = case_when(
    method == "biaee"       ~ "BiAAE",
    method == "bicev"       ~ "BiCEV",
    method == "fame"        ~ "FAME",
    method == "gex2sgen"    ~ "Gex2SGen",
    method == "gexmolgen"   ~ "GexMolGen",
    method == "gxrnn"       ~ "GxRNN",
    method == "paccmann_rl" ~ "Paccmann RL",
    method == "smilesgen"   ~ "SmilesGEN",
    method == "transgem"    ~ "TransGEM",
    method == "triomphe"    ~ "TRIOMPHE",
    TRUE                    ~ method # Keeps any unexpected values as-is
  ))
gen_metrics <- gen_metrics %>%  
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup()
data = df%>%inner_join(gen_metrics, by = "method")
data <- data %>% rownames_to_column("id")
colnames(data) <- c(
  "id", "method", "QED", "SA score", "MW", "LogP", "HBA", "HBD", 
  "Safety", "Tanimoto Similarity", "Internal Energy", "Internal Steric Clash",  
  "Aromatic Ring Flatness", "Non Aromatic Ring Flatness", "Short Bond Outliers", 
  "Long Bond Outliers", "Extreme Angle", "DRS", "Validity", "Uniqueness", 
  "Novelty", "Diversity"
)

data$DRS <- (data$DRS + 1)/2
#  Define Column Information
library(tibble)

column_info <- tribble(
  ~id,                          ~group,        ~name,                       ~geom,       ~palette,              ~options,
  "method",                     "General",     "",                          "text",      "Method",              list(width = 2),
  "Validity",                   "Generative",  "Validity",                  "funkyrect", "Generative metrics",  lst(),
  "Uniqueness",                 "Generative",  "Uniqueness",                "funkyrect", "Generative metrics",  lst(),
  "Novelty",                    "Generative",  "Novelty",                   "funkyrect", "Generative metrics",  list(width = 1, scale = FALSE),
  "Diversity",                  "Generative",  "Diversity",                 "funkyrect", "Generative metrics",  lst(),
  "Safety",                     "Chemical",    "Safety",                    "bar",       "Drug-like metrics",   list(width = 1, draw_outline = FALSE, scale = FALSE),
  "QED",                        "Chemical",    "QED",                       "bar",       "Drug-like metrics",   list(width = 1, draw_outline = FALSE, scale = FALSE),
  "SA score",                   "Chemical",    "SA score",                  "bar",       "Drug-like metrics",   list(width = 1, draw_outline = FALSE),
  "MW",                         "Chemical",    "MW",                        "bar", "Drug-like metrics",   list(width = 1, draw_outline = FALSE),
  "LogP",                       "Chemical",    "LogP",                      "bar", "Drug-like metrics",   list(width = 1, draw_outline = FALSE),
  "HBA",                        "Chemical",    "HBA",                       "bar", "Drug-like metrics",   list(width = 1, draw_outline = FALSE),
  "HBD",                        "Chemical",    "HBD",                       "bar", "Drug-like metrics",   list(width = 1, draw_outline = FALSE),
  
  "Tanimoto Similarity",        "Structural",  "Tanimoto Similarity",       "funkyrect",       "Structural metrics", list(width = 1, legend = FALSE, draw_outline = FALSE, scale = FALSE),
  
  "Internal Energy",            "Structural",  "Internal Energy",           "funkyrect",    "Structural metrics",  list(width = 1, scale = FALSE),
  "Internal Steric Clash",      "Structural",  "Internal Steric Clash",     "funkyrect",    "Structural metrics",  list(width = 1, scale = FALSE),
  
  "Aromatic Ring Flatness",     "Structural",  "Aromatic Ring Flatness",    "funkyrect",    "Structural metrics",  list(legend = FALSE, draw_outline = FALSE, scale = FALSE),
  "Non Aromatic Ring Flatness", "Structural",  "Non Aromatic Ring Flatness","funkyrect",    "Structural metrics",  list(legend = FALSE, draw_outline = FALSE, scale = FALSE),
  "Short Bond Outliers",        "Structural",  "Short Bond Outliers",       "funkyrect",    "Structural metrics",  list(width = 1, scale = FALSE),
  "Long Bond Outliers",         "Structural",  "Long Bond Outliers",        "funkyrect",    "Structural metrics",  list(width = 1, scale = FALSE),
  "Extreme Angle",              "Structural",  "Extreme Angle",             "funkyrect",    "Structural metrics",  list(width = 1, scale = TRUE),
  
  "DRS",                        "Biological",  "DRS",                       "circle",       "Disease Reversal",    list(legend = FALSE, draw_outline = FALSE, scale = FALSE, width = 4)
)

# 2. Define Column Groups
column_groups <- tribble(
  ~group,        ~name,                      ~palette,
  "General",     "Method",                   "Method",
  "Generative",  "Generative",   "Generative metrics",
  "Chemical",    "Drug-like",                "Drug-like metrics",
  "Structural",  "Structural",    "Structural metrics",
  "Biological",  "Disease Reversal",         "Disease Reversal",
)

# Define palettes for your stages

# 5. Define Palettes using exact purple, blue, pink, and neutral shades matching your reference figure
palettes <- list(
   Method = "skyblue",
  `Generative metrics`    = c("#F1F8FE", "#C5D4E6", "#8C9AC2", "#7B3F9B", "#4A0E4E") , # Clean blue gradient
  `Drug-like metrics`     = c("#FFF0EE", "#FADBD8", "#F46095", "#A7007A", "#3A054F"), # Deep purple gradient (matching reference batch correction blocks)
  `Structural metrics`    = "Greens", # Rich pink/magenta gradient (matching reference bio conservation blocks)
  `Disease Reversal`      = "YlOrBr" # Red gradient
)

legends <- list(
  list(palette = "Generative metrics", geom = "funkyrect", title = "Generative metrics"),
  list(palette = "Drug-like metrics", geom = "bar", title = "Drug-like metrics"),
  list(palette = "Structural metrics", geom = "circle", title = "Structural metrics")
)

plot <- funky_heatmap(
    data = data,
    column_info = column_info,
    column_groups = column_groups,
    palettes = palettes,
    legends = legends,
    position_args = position_arguments(
        col_annot_angle = 35,
        expand_ymin = 3,
        col_annot_offset = 1
    )
)


main <- plot[[1]]

# Confirm layer order fresh
# for (i in seq_along(main$layers)) cat(i, ":", class(main$layers[[i]]$geom)[1], "\n")

# Confirm no duplicate GeomText layers this time
text_layers <- which(sapply(main$layers, function(l) class(l$geom)[1]) == "GeomText")
# text_layers
# length(text_layers) == 1 

T <- text_layers[1]

d <- main$layers[[T]]$data
# table(d$angle)   # should now show 0 and 90, not 0 and 30

is_header <- d$angle == 35
row_bg <- main$layers[[which(sapply(main$layers, function(l) class(l$geom)[1]) == "GeomRect")[1]]]$data
min_y  <- min(row_bg$ymin, na.rm = TRUE)

d$y[is_header]     <- min_y - 1
d$hjust[is_header] <- 1.1
d$vjust[is_header] <- 1
main$layers[[T]]$data <- d


d3 <- main$layers[[3]]$data

bars <- d3[!(abs(d3$ymin - 3) < 0.01 & abs(d3$ymax - 4) < 0.01), ]

bar_layer <- ggplot2::geom_rect(
  data = bars,
  mapping = ggplot2::aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = colour),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  colour = NA
)
group_order <- unique(column_info$group)

hd <- d3[abs(d3$ymin - 1) < 0.01 & abs(d3$ymax - 2) < 0.01, ]

hd <- hd[order(hd$xmin), ]
hd$group <- group_order
hd$name  <- column_groups$name[match(hd$group, column_groups$group)]

# hd[, c("xmin", "xmax", "colour", "group", "name")]
hd <- hd[order(hd$xmin), ]
hd$group <- group_order
hd$name  <- column_groups$name[match(hd$group, column_groups$group)]

# hd[, c("xmin", "xmax", "colour", "group", "name")]
hd$radius <- 0.3
header_layer <- funkyheatmap::geom_rounded_rect(
  data = hd,
  mapping = ggplot2::aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, radius = 0.3),
  fill = hd$colour,
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

main$layers[[3]] <- bar_layer
main$layers <- append(main$layers, list(header_layer), after = 3)

hd$x_mid <- (hd$xmin + hd$xmax) / 2
hd$y_mid <- (hd$ymin + hd$ymax) / 2

main <- main + ggplot2::geom_text(
  data = hd,
  mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = x_mid, y = y_mid, label = name),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  colour = "white",
  fontface = "bold",
  size = 4
)


d5 <- main$layers[[7]]$data

header_names <- hd$name   # the 6 group names you already confirmed

d5_clean <- d5[!(d5$label_value %in% header_names), ]

# nrow(d5)        # before
# nrow(d5_clean)  # should be exactly 6 fewer

main$layers[[7]]$data <- d5_clean
main$layers[[2]] <- NULL

plot[[1]] <- main
plot
```

## Stringent staged evaluation reveals substantial attrition in generated molecules

1.  There is substantive attrition across multiple evaluation stages (@fig-2)

2.  Performance at one evaluation stage does not reliably predict performance at the next, revealing complementary failure modes that single-stage benchmarks obscure (@fig-4, @fig-3)

::: panel-tabset
### Attrition rate across Theraflow stages

```{r}
#| label: fig-2
#| fig-width: 10

raw = fread("outputs/merged_master_dataframe.csv")
data = raw
external_totals = data %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    Total    = n())

# 1. Calculate the cumulative percentage of molecules PASSING each tier
df_passing <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    pass_Basic_Chem = sanitization & all_atoms_connected & passes_valence_checks & passes_kekulization,
    pass_Geometry   = bond_lengths & bond_angles & (number_clashes == 0),
    pass_Planarity  = aromatic_ring_flatness & double_bond_flatness,
    pass_PoseBusters_Total = pass_Basic_Chem & pass_Geometry & pass_Planarity
  ) %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    `Candidate molecules` = 100,
    `Syntactic validation`       = sum(!is.na(QED)),
    `Medicinal Chemistry Validation`  = sum(!is.na(bond_angles)) ,
    `Structural validation`      = sum(pass_PoseBusters_Total, na.rm = T),
    `Functional and Biological validation`  = sum(!is.na(reversal_score_scaled)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(external_totals, by = "method") %>%
    mutate(
    `Candidate molecules`                  = 100,
    `Syntactic validation`                  = `Syntactic validation` / Total * 100,
    `Medicinal Chemistry Validation`       = `Medicinal Chemistry Validation` / Total * 100,
    `Structural validation`                 = `Structural validation` / Total * 100,
    `Functional and Biological validation` = `Functional and Biological validation` / Total * 100
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Total) %>%
  # Convert to long format for ggplot
  pivot_longer(cols = -method, names_to = "Pipeline_Stage", values_to = "Percentage")



# Ensure the pipeline stages maintain their chronological order on the plot
df_passing$Pipeline_Stage <- factor(
  df_passing$Pipeline_Stage, 
  levels = df_passing$Pipeline_Stage%>%unique()
)

# 2. Create the Stacked Bar Chart (Using position = "identity" or side-by-side dodge)
# Note: For passing rates, an "identity" overlay or a "dodge" (side-by-side) bar 
# is mathematically cleaner than stacking them on top of each other, 
# as Stage 4 is already a subset of Stage 3.
ggplot(df_passing, aes(x = method, y = Percentage, fill = Pipeline_Stage)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.8, color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) + 
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Methods",
    y = "Pass rate (%)",
    fill = "Stage"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

### Drug-Like and Structural Pass Rates for Valid Molecules

```{r}
#| label: fig-3
df = raw

method_colors <- c(
  "BiAAE"       = "#ff9999",
  "BiCEV"       = "#ffbb99",
  "FAME"        = "#ffecb3",
  "Gex2SGen"    = "#ffffcc",
  "GexMolGen"   = "#d4edda",
  "GxRNN"       = "#a3e4d7",
  "Paccmann RL" = "#a9cce3",
  "SmilesGEN"   = "#bb8fce",
  "TransGEM"    = "#d7bde2",
  "TRIOMPHE"    = "#f5b7b1"
)


# 1. add posebusters pass and subset the dataframe to only include molecules with valid 3D conformations
conformer_df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    pass_Basic_Chem = sanitization & all_atoms_connected & passes_valence_checks & passes_kekulization,
    pass_Geometry   = bond_lengths & bond_angles & (number_clashes == 0),
    pass_Planarity  = aromatic_ring_flatness & double_bond_flatness,
    pass_PoseBusters_Total = pass_Basic_Chem & pass_Geometry & pass_Planarity
  ) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(pass_PoseBusters_Total))  # subset here

# 2. Calculate the passing counts and percentages for each metric
pass_rate_summary <- conformer_df %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Conformers = n(),
    Count_Druglike  = sum((QED > 0.5) & (SA_Score < 4.5) & (MW < 500) & (LogP < 5) & (HBA <= 10) & (HBD <= 5), na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_Structural = sum(pass_PoseBusters_Total, na.rm = T),
    
    # Percent Pass Rates (%)
    Pct_Druglike     = (Count_Druglike / Total_Conformers) * 100,
    Pct_Structural  = (Count_Structural / Total_Conformers) * 100,
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Pivot the counts into long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Count_") | starts_with("Pct_"),
    names_to = c(".value", "Metric"),
    names_pattern = "(Count|Pct)_(.*)"
  )

ggplot(pass_rate_summary, aes(x = Metric, y = Pct, fill = method)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, color = "black", size = 0.1) +
  # Add absolute molecule counts as text labels on top of the bars
  geom_text(
    aes(label = Count), 
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
    vjust = -0.4, 
    size = 3, 
    fontface = "bold",
    lineheight = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  ylim(0, 115) + # Add padding at the top for labels
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
    x = "Methods",
    y = "Pass rate (%) among molecules \n satisfying Lipinski Rule of 5",
    fill = "Generative Method"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

### Structural vs Drug-like

```{r}
#| label: fig-4

data = raw
external_totals = data %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Gen    = n())

# 1. Calculate the counts from your raw data
drug_like_analysis <- raw %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    # Raw passing counts for each individual gate
    Stage1_Valid = sum(!is.na(QED)),
    Stage2_Valid = sum((MW < 500) & 
                         (LogP < 5) & (HBA <= 10) & (HBD <= 5), na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_druglike = sum((QED > 0.5) & (SA_Score < 4.5) & (MW < 500) & (LogP < 5) & (HBA <= 10) & (HBD <= 5), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # 2. Pivot to long format so we can handle metrics cleanly
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Count_"),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Passed_Count"
  ) %>%
  # 3. Merge/Join with your external totals dataframe
  left_join(external_totals, by = "method") %>%
  # 4. Clean metric names and calculate pass rates using the external denominators
  mutate(
    Metric = gsub("Count_", "", Metric),
    Pass_Rate_Total  = (Passed_Count / Total_Gen) * 100,    # X-axis
    Pass_Rate_Stage1 = (Passed_Count / Stage1_Valid) * 100, # Y-axis
    Pass_Rate_Stage2 = (Passed_Count / Stage2_Valid) * 100
  )

p1 = ggplot(drug_like_analysis, aes(x = Pass_Rate_Total, y = Pass_Rate_Stage1, color = method, size = Passed_Count)) +
  # Map the Stage 2 conditional pass rate to both color intensity and dot size
  geom_point(aes(color = Pass_Rate_Stage2, size = Passed_Count, shape = method), stroke = 1.5) +

  # Styling the visuals
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(4:13)) + # Different shapes for different PB constraints
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = c("#9ecae1", "#de2d26"),
    name = "Drug-like molecules"
  ) + 
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8), name = "Count") +
  
  xlim(0, 100) + ylim(0, 110) + # Added slight ceiling padding for text labels
  theme_classic(base_size = 15) +
  labs(
    x = "Lipinski Rule of 5 (Stage 2) pass from Total Generated Set (%)",
    y = "Lipinski Rule of 5 (Stage 2) pass from Stage 1 Syntax (%)"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )


# 1. Calculate the three specific denominators for each PoseBusters metric
posebusters_analysis <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    # Basic Chemistry Check
    pass_Basic_Chem = sanitization & all_atoms_connected & passes_valence_checks & passes_kekulization,
    
    # Core Geometric Realism
    pass_Geometry   = bond_lengths & bond_angles & (number_clashes == 0),
    
    # Flatness Requirements
    pass_Planarity  = aromatic_ring_flatness & double_bond_flatness,
    
    # The Definitive PoseBusters Pass (Must clear everything)
    pass_PoseBusters_Total = pass_Basic_Chem & pass_Geometry & pass_Planarity
  ) %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    # Baselines
    Stage1_Valid = sum(!is.na(QED)),
    Stage2_Valid = sum((MW < 500) & 
                       (LogP < 5) & (HBA <= 10) & (HBD <= 5), na.rm = TRUE),
    Passed_Count   = sum(pass_PoseBusters_Total == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(external_totals, by = "method") %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate your three distinct dimensions of performance
    Pass_Rate_Total  = (Passed_Count / Total_Gen) * 100,     # X-axis
    Pass_Rate_Stage1 = (Passed_Count / Stage1_Valid) * 100,   # Y-axis
    Pass_Rate_Stage2 = (Passed_Count / Stage2_Valid) * 100    # Color & Size
  )

# 3. Generate the Multidimensional 2D Scatter Plot
p2 = ggplot(posebusters_analysis, aes(x = Pass_Rate_Total, y = Pass_Rate_Stage1)) +
  # Map the Stage 2 conditional pass rate to both color intensity and dot size
  geom_point(aes(color = Pass_Rate_Stage2, size = Passed_Count, shape = method), stroke = 1.5) +

  # Styling the visuals
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(4:13)) + # Different shapes for different PB constraint
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = c("#9ecae1", "#de2d26"),
    name = "Drug-like molecules"
  ) + 
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8), name = "Count") +
  
  xlim(0, 100) + ylim(0, 110) + # Added slight ceiling padding for text labels
  theme_classic(base_size = 15) +
  labs(
    x = "Structural (Stage 3) Pass from Total Generated Set (%)",
    y = "Structural (Stage 3) Pass from Stage 1 Syntax (%)"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )




# now compare the attrition rate in stage 1 and stage 2 between the two dataframes 
# 1. Join the two analyses on method (each already has Pass_Rate_Total/Stage1/Stage2)
combined <- drug_like_analysis %>%
  dplyr::select(method, 
         DrugLike_Total  = Pass_Rate_Total, 
         DrugLike_Stage1 = Pass_Rate_Stage1, 
         DrugLike_Stage2 = Pass_Rate_Stage2,   # note: your drug_like_analysis names this differently, adjust if needed
         DrugLike_Count  = Passed_Count) %>%
  inner_join(
    posebusters_analysis %>%
      dplyr::select(method, 
             Structural_Total  = Pass_Rate_Total, 
             Structural_Stage1 = Pass_Rate_Stage1, 
             Structural_Stage2 = Pass_Rate_Stage2,
             Structural_Count  = Passed_Count),
    by = "method"
  )

# 2. Reshape into long format so ggplot can facet by "Stage"
combined_long <- combined %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(DrugLike_Total, DrugLike_Stage1, DrugLike_Stage2,
             Structural_Total, Structural_Stage1, Structural_Stage2),
    names_to = c("Metric", "Stage"),
    names_pattern = "(DrugLike|Structural)_(.*)",
    values_to = "Pass_Rate"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Metric,
    values_from = Pass_Rate
  ) %>%
  mutate(Stage = factor(Stage, levels = c("Total", "Stage1", "Stage2"),
                         labels = c("vs Total Generated", "vs Stage 1 Syntax-Valid", "vs Stage 2 Med-Chem-Valid")))

# 3. One faceted plot: DrugLike (x) vs Structural (y), one panel per stage
ggplot(combined_long, aes(x = DrugLike, y = Structural, fill = method, size = DrugLike_Count)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "maroon") +
  facet_wrap(~ Stage, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8), name = "Count") +
  xlim(0, 100) + ylim(0, 100) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
    x = "Drug-like Pass Rate (%)",
    y = "Structural (PoseBusters) Pass Rate (%)",
    color = "Generative Method"
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-6
data = raw

ext_data = raw

external_totals = ext_data %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    N_total    = n()) 

# ==============================================================================
# 1. GENERATE THE SOURCE DATA (drug_like_funnel)
# ==============================================================================

# A. Compute Base Denominators for the 2D layer
s2_denominators <- data %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(                              # Total initial generations (Stage 0)
    N_valid  = sum(is.na(QED)),                   # Syntax valid (where QED was successfully computed)
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(external_totals, by = "method")
  

# B. Compute Passing Volumes and Multi-Baseline Rates (Including HBA and HBD)
drug_like_funnel <- data %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    Count_QED   = sum(QED > 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_SA    = sum(SA_Score < 4.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_MW    = sum(MW < 500, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_LogP  = sum(LogP < 5, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_TPSA  = sum(TPSA < 140, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_HBA   = sum(HBA <= 10, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_HBD   = sum(HBD <= 5, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(s2_denominators, by = "method") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Count_"), 
    names_to = "Metric", 
    values_to = "Passed_Count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Metric = gsub("Count_", "", Metric),
    # Compute your 2 target baseline columns
    total_pass_rate  = (Passed_Count / N_total) * 100,   # (Passed / Total Generated)
    syntax_pass_rate = (Passed_Count / N_valid) * 100    # (Passed / Syntax Valid)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(method, Metric, total_pass_rate, syntax_pass_rate)


# ==============================================================================
# 2. TRANSFORM AND PLOT THE RIBBON GRAPHICS
# ==============================================================================

# A. Shape the data into a long plotting layout
plot1_ribbon_data <- drug_like_funnel %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(total_pass_rate, syntax_pass_rate),
    names_to = "Baseline",
    values_to = "Rate"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Baseline = factor(Baseline, levels = c("total_pass_rate", "syntax_pass_rate"),
                      labels = c("Entire Library (Total)", "Syntax Valid Only")),
    # Explicitly define factor levels to control subplot sequence ordering
    Metric = factor(Metric, levels = c("QED", "SA", "MW", "LogP", "TPSA", "HBA", "HBD"))
  )

# B. Calculate intermediate gap locations for mid-ribbon text annotations
gap_annotations <- drug_like_funnel %>%
  mutate(
    Gap = syntax_pass_rate - total_pass_rate,
    Mid_X = (syntax_pass_rate + total_pass_rate) / 2,
    Metric = factor(Metric, levels = c("QED", "SA", "MW", "LogP", "TPSA", "HBA", "HBD"))
  )

# C. Generate the exact ribbon dot plot configuration
ggplot() +
  # Draw the gray horizontal ribbon tracking the baseline gap
  geom_segment(data = drug_like_funnel,
               aes(x = total_pass_rate, xend = syntax_pass_rate, y = method, yend = method), 
               color = "grey80", linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Baseline 1: All generated background baseline (Orange Circle)
  geom_point(data = filter(plot1_ribbon_data, Baseline == "Entire Library (Total)"),
             aes(x = Rate, y = method, color = Baseline), size = 4, shape = 16) +
  
  # Baseline 2: Conditional syntax-valid baseline (Blue Triangle)
  geom_point(data = filter(plot1_ribbon_data, Baseline == "Syntax Valid Only"),
             aes(x = Rate, y = method, color = Baseline), size = 3, shape = 17) +
  
  # # Overlay the numerical Gap value on top of the gray ribbon segments
  # geom_text(data = gap_annotations,
  #           aes(x = Mid_X, y = method, label = sprintf("%.1f", Gap)), 
  #           vjust = -0.6, size = 2.8, colour = "grey30", fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Grid splittings based on the 7 explicit physicochemical filters
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, ncol = 4) +

  # Consistent color schema matching your pipeline
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Entire Library (Total)" = "firebrick", "Syntax Valid Only" = "steelblue")) +
  xlim(0, 105) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "Method", 
    x = "Pass Rate (%) from"
  )



# 1. Compute Base Denominators (Including the new Stage 2 Drug-like Anchor)
s3_denominators <- data %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    N_valid    = sum(!is.na(QED)),
    N_druglike = sum((QED > 0.5) & (SA_Score < 4.5) & (MW < 500) & (LogP < 5), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(external_totals, by = "method")

# 2. Add structural flags and aggregate passing rates across all 3 denominators
posebusters_funnel <- data %>%
  mutate(
    pass_Basic_Chem = sanitization & all_atoms_connected & passes_valence_checks & passes_kekulization,
    pass_Geometry   = bond_lengths & bond_angles & (number_clashes == 0),
    pass_Planarity  = aromatic_ring_flatness & double_bond_flatness,
    pass_Total = pass_Basic_Chem & pass_Geometry & pass_Planarity
  ) %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    Count_Basic_Structure   = sum(pass_Basic_Chem == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_Geometry     = sum(pass_Geometry == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_Planarity    = sum(pass_Planarity == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    Count_Total  = sum(pass_Total == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(s3_denominators, by = "method") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Count_"), 
    names_to = "Metric", 
    values_to = "Passed_Count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Metric = gsub("Count_", "", Metric),
    # Compute your 3 target columns
    total_pass_rate     = (Passed_Count / N_total) * 100,
    syntax_pass_rate    = (Passed_Count / N_valid) * 100,
    drug_like_pass_rate = (Passed_Count / N_druglike) * 100
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(method, Metric, total_pass_rate, syntax_pass_rate, drug_like_pass_rate)


# 1. Shape the 3D data into a long plotting format
plot2_ribbon_data <- posebusters_funnel %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(total_pass_rate, syntax_pass_rate, drug_like_pass_rate),
    names_to = "Baseline",
    values_to = "Rate"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Baseline = factor(Baseline, 
                      levels = c("total_pass_rate", "syntax_pass_rate", "drug_like_pass_rate"),
                      labels = c("Entire Library (Total)", "Syntax Valid Only", "Medchem Passed"))
  )
```

## Distinct generative architectures occupy different regions of therapeutic evaluation space

Comparing all syntactically valid molecules with the Pareto-optimal subset revealed distinct performance profiles across architectures @fig-8

### Performance profile

```{r}
#| label: fig-8
#| fig-height: 10
# combining the geometric metrics to reduce dimensionality 
set.seed(42)
safe_div <- function(a, b) {
  ifelse(is.na(b) | b == 0, 0, a / b)
}

clip01 <- function(x) {
  pmin(pmax(x, 0), 1)
}

normalize_count <- function(x, cap) {
  clip01(x / cap)
}

df = raw

df <- df %>%
  mutate(

    # -------------------------
    # structural validity
    # -------------------------
    structural_validity = rowMeans(cbind(
      as.numeric(inchi_convertible),
      as.numeric(all_atoms_connected),
      as.numeric(no_radicals),
      safe_div(number_valid_bonds, number_bonds),
      safe_div(number_valid_angles, number_angles),
      safe_div(number_valid_noncov_pairs, number_noncov_pairs)
    ), na.rm = TRUE),

    # -------------------------
    # bond + angle consistency
    # Having 10 completely distorted outlier bonds means a massive fraction ($20\%$ to $50\%$) of the entire  molecule's backbone is chemically deformed. Setting the cap at 10 isolates this severe, systemic geometry failure.
    # -------------------------
    bond_angle_consistency = 1 - clip01(
      (normalize_count(number_short_outlier_bonds, 10) +
       normalize_count(number_long_outlier_bonds, 10) +
       normalize_count(number_outlier_angles, 10)) / 3
    ),

    # -------------------------
    # steric feasibility
    # -------------------------
    steric_feasibility = 1 - clip01(
      (normalize_count(number_clashes, 10) +
       normalize_count(number_noncov_pairs, 20)) / 2
    ),

  # Non-Covalent Pairs: Non-covalent pairs represent close-contact interactions (like Van der Waals clashes or steric overlaps) between atoms that aren't directly bonded. Because every atom can potentially clash with multiple neighboring atoms, a poorly optimized 3D conformation can easily rack up dozens of unfavorable close contacts. A threshold of 10 would be crossed too easily by mild structural crowding, whereas 20 severe clashes represents a catastrophic packing failure.
    # -------------------------
    # ring planarity
    # -------------------------
    ring_planarity = rowMeans(cbind(

      safe_div(number_aromatic_rings_pass,
               number_aromatic_rings_checked),

      safe_div(`number_non-aromatic_rings_pass`,
               `number_non-aromatic_rings_checked`),

      1 - clip01(aromatic_ring_maximum_distance_from_plane / 1),

      1 - clip01(`non-aromatic_ring_maximum_distance_from_plane` / 1)

    ), na.rm = TRUE),

    # -------------------------
    # double bond geometry
    # -------------------------
    double_bond_geometry = rowMeans(cbind(

      safe_div(number_double_bonds_pass,
               number_double_bonds_checked),

      1 - clip01(double_bond_maximum_distance_from_plane / 1)

    ), na.rm = TRUE)

  )

# Sanitization 
meta  <- fread("method_processing/data/metrics_metadata.csv")
selected_metrics = meta[Classification == "Chemical validity",]$Metric 

df <- df %>%
  mutate(weighted_sanitization = rowMeans(across(all_of(selected_metrics)), na.rm = TRUE))

selected_metrics <- c(
  "QED", "SA_Score", "MW", "LogP", "TPSA", "HBA", "HBD", "F_Csp3",
  "structural_validity", "bond_angle_consistency", "steric_feasibility", 
  "double_bond_geometry", "weighted_sanitization", "Sim_Morg_Tani", 
  "energy_ratio", 'ensemble_avg_energy', 'reversal_score_scaled'
)

# df_clean <- df %>%
#   drop_na(all_of(selected_metrics))


df_ready <- df %>%
  filter(
    number_clashes == 0 & Passes_Safety == TRUE
  ) # optimize for pareto (needs to be noted clearly in the methods)

p_11d <- high(QED) * low(SA_Score) * low(MW) * low(LogP) * low(TPSA) * low(HBA) * low(HBD) * high(bond_angle_consistency) * high(steric_feasibility) * high(double_bond_geometry) * high(weighted_sanitization) * high(Sim_Morg_Tani) * low(energy_ratio)* low(ensemble_avg_energy) * high(F_Csp3) * high(reversal_score_scaled)

pareto_11d_results <- psel(df_ready, p_11d, top = nrow(df_ready))

top <- pareto_11d_results %>%
  filter(.level == 1)

radar_pillars_df <- top %>%
  # 1. First, normalize individual metrics on a 0-1 scale across the whole dataset 
  mutate(
    # Inversions (Higher must equal better/more optimized)
    norm_QED                  = rescale(QED, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_SA                   = rescale(10 - SA_Score, to = c(0, 1)), # Higher = easier to synthesize
    norm_MW                   = rescale(MW, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_LogP                 = rescale(LogP, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_TPSA                 = rescale(TPSA, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_HBA                  = rescale(HBA, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_HBD                  = rescale(HBD, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_F_Csp3               = rescale(F_Csp3, to = c(0, 1)),
    
    norm_structural_validity  = rescale(structural_validity, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_bond_consistency     = rescale(bond_angle_consistency, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_steric_feasibility   = rescale(steric_feasibility, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_double_bond          = rescale(double_bond_geometry, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_sanitization         = rescale(weighted_sanitization, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_similarity           = Sim_Morg_Tani,
    
    norm_energy_ratio         = rescale(energy_ratio, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_energy_stability     = rescale(-1 * ensemble_avg_energy, to = c(0, 1)) # Higher = more stable
  ) %>%
  # 2. Construct the 3 requested macro-pillars by calculating row means per molecule
  mutate(
    `Drug-likeness` = rowMeans(cbind(
      norm_QED, norm_SA, norm_MW, norm_LogP, norm_TPSA, norm_HBA, norm_HBD, norm_F_Csp3
    ), na.rm = TRUE),
    
    `Structural Properties` = rowMeans(cbind(
      norm_structural_validity, norm_bond_consistency, norm_steric_feasibility, 
      norm_double_bond, norm_sanitization
    ), na.rm = TRUE),
    
    `Energy (Molecular Dynamics)` = rowMeans(cbind(
      norm_energy_ratio, norm_energy_stability
    ), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # 3. Collapse the data down to the individual Method averages
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    `Drug-likeness`               = mean(`Drug-likeness`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Structural Properties`       = mean(`Structural Properties`, na.rm = TRUE),
     Energy = mean(`Energy (Molecular Dynamics)`, na.rm = TRUE),
     DRS = mean(reversal_score_scaled, na.rm = TRUE),
     Similarity = mean(norm_similarity)
  ) %>%
  # 4. Final safety rescaling to guarantee the geometry spans exactly 0 to 1
  mutate(across(-method, rescale, to = c(0, 1)))

radar_pillars_df[, -1][is.na(radar_pillars_df[, -1])] <- 0

# 5. Generate the 3-axis Radar Plot
```

```{r}
cov_dat <- top %>%
  # 1. First, normalize individual metrics on a 0-1 scale across the whole dataset 
  mutate(
    # Inversions (Higher must equal better/more optimized)
    norm_QED                  = rescale(QED, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_SA                   = rescale(10 - SA_Score, to = c(0, 1)), # Higher = easier to synthesize
    norm_MW                   = rescale(MW, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_LogP                 = rescale(LogP, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_TPSA                 = rescale(TPSA, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_HBA                  = rescale(HBA, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_HBD                  = rescale(HBD, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_F_Csp3               = rescale(F_Csp3, to = c(0, 1)),
    
    norm_structural_validity  = rescale(structural_validity, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_bond_consistency     = rescale(bond_angle_consistency, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_steric_feasibility   = rescale(steric_feasibility, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_double_bond          = rescale(double_bond_geometry, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_sanitization         = rescale(weighted_sanitization, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_similarity           = Sim_Morg_Tani,
    
    norm_energy_ratio         = rescale(energy_ratio, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_energy_stability     = rescale(-1 * ensemble_avg_energy, to = c(0, 1)) # Higher = more stable
  )

individual_metrics <- c(
  "norm_QED", "norm_SA", "norm_MW", "norm_LogP", "norm_TPSA", "norm_HBA", "norm_HBD", "norm_F_Csp3",
  "norm_structural_validity", "norm_bond_consistency", "norm_steric_feasibility", "norm_double_bond", "norm_sanitization",
  "norm_energy_ratio", "norm_energy_stability",
  "reversal_score_scaled", "norm_similarity"
)

global_cov <- cov(cov_dat[, ..individual_metrics], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# 3. Fix your Method List calculation
cov_list <- cov_dat %>%
  split(by = "method") %>%
  map(function(d) {
    # Force subsetting down to JUST the numeric metrics vector before running cov()
    cov(d[, ..individual_metrics], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  })


plot_data_absolute <- imap_dfr(cov_list, function(cov_mat, arch_name) {
  
  # Turn the matrix into a table/dataframe directly without subtraction
  as.data.frame(as.table(cov_mat)) %>%
    rename(
      class1 = Var1,
      class2 = Var2,
      abs_cov = Freq # Keeping track that this is absolute covariance
    ) %>%
    mutate(method = arch_name)
})


plot_data_low <- plot_data_absolute %>%
  mutate(across(c(class1, class2), ~ . %>%
                str_remove_all("norm_") %>%
                str_replace_all("_", " ") %>%
                tools::toTitleCase()
  )) %>%
  # This keeping condition forces the lower triangle layout
  filter(as.character(class1) >= as.character(class2))

finite_vals <- plot_data_low$abs_cov[is.finite(plot_data_low$abs_cov)]
cov_range <- quantile(finite_vals, probs = c(0.01, 0.99))
dynamic_breaks <- seq(
  from = cov_range[1], 
  to = cov_range[2], 
  length.out = 6
)


# Assuming plot_data_low is already filtered for the lower triangle
ggplot(plot_data_low, aes(x = class1, y = class2, fill = abs_cov)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) + 
  facet_wrap(~method, nrow = 2) + 
  # Use a binned scale tailored exactly to your dense low-value distribution
  scale_fill_stepsn(
  colors = c("#e0f3f8", "#abd9e9", "#bfd3e6", "#9ebcda", "#8c96c6", "#8c6bb1", "#810f7c"),
  breaks = dynamic_breaks,
  labels = round(dynamic_breaks, 3),
  limits = cov_range,

)+

    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7)
  ) +
  labs(
    fill = "Absolute\nCovariance",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  coord_fixed()

    norm_MW                   = rescale(MW, to = c(0, 1)),
```

```{r}
    norm_F_Csp3               = rescale(F_Csp3, to = c(0, 1)),
    
    norm_structural_validity  = rescale(structural_validity, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_bond_consistency     = rescale(bond_angle_consistency, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_steric_feasibility   = rescale(steric_feasibility, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_double_bond          = rescale(double_bond_geometry, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_sanitization         = rescale(weighted_sanitization, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_similarity           = Sim_Morg_Tani,
    
    norm_energy_ratio         = rescale(energy_ratio, to = c(0, 1)),
    norm_energy_stability     = rescale(-1 * ensemble_avg_energy, to = c(0, 1)) # Higher = more stable
  )

individual_metrics <- c(
  "norm_QED", "norm_SA", "norm_MW", "norm_LogP", "norm_TPSA", "norm_HBA", "norm_HBD", "norm_F_Csp3",
  "norm_structural_validity", "norm_bond_consistency", "norm_steric_feasibility", "norm_double_bond", "norm_sanitization",
  "norm_energy_ratio", "norm_energy_stability",
  "reversal_score_scaled", "norm_similarity"
)

architecture_complexity <- read_csv("method_processing/data/architecture_complexity.csv")
architecture_complexity <- architecture_complexity %>%
  mutate(method = case_when(
    method == "biaee"       ~ "BiAAE",
    method == "bicev"       ~ "BiCEV",
    method == "fame"        ~ "FAME",
    method == "gex2sgen"    ~ "Gex2SGen",
    method == "gexmolgen"   ~ "GexMolGen",
    method == "gxrnn"       ~ "GxRNN",
    method == "paccmann_rl" ~ "Paccmann RL",
    method == "smilesgen"   ~ "SmilesGEN",
    method == "transgem"    ~ "TransGEM",
    method == "triomphe"    ~ "TRIOMPHE",
    TRUE                    ~ method # Keeps any unexpected values as-is
  ))
top_df = inner_join(top,architecture_complexity, by = "method")

method_metric_df <- top_df %>% mutate(
    # Inversions (Higher must equal better/more optimized)
    QED                  = rescale(QED, to = c(0, 1)),
    SA                   = rescale(10 - SA_Score, to = c(0, 1)), # Higher = easier to synthesize
    MW                   = rescale(MW, to = c(0, 1)),
    LogP                 = rescale(LogP, to = c(0, 1)),
    TPSA                 = rescale(TPSA, to = c(0, 1)),
    HBA                  = rescale(HBA, to = c(0, 1)),
    HBD                  = rescale(HBD, to = c(0, 1)),
    F_Csp3               = rescale(F_Csp3, to = c(0, 1)),
    
    structural_validity  = rescale(structural_validity, to = c(0, 1)),
    steric_feasibility   = rescale(steric_feasibility, to = c(0, 1)),
    double_bond          = rescale(double_bond_geometry, to = c(0, 1)),
    sanitization         = rescale(weighted_sanitization, to = c(0, 1)),
    similarity           = Sim_Morg_Tani,
    DRS = reversal_score_scaled) %>%
    group_by(method) %>%
    summarise(
        across(
            c(QED, SA, MW, LogP, TPSA,
              HBA, HBD, F_Csp3,
              similarity,
              DRS),
            ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        ),
        across(
            c(structural_validity,
             steric_feasibility,
              double_bond,
              sanitization),
            ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
    )

metric_mat <- method_metric_df %>%
  column_to_rownames("method") %>%
  as.matrix()

metric_mat_scaled <- metric_mat
metric_mat_scaled <- t(metric_mat_scaled)

# --- 1. Data Preparation ---
# (Assuming method_metric_df, metric_mat_scaled, and annotation_df are prepared as per our previous logic)

row_groups <- c(
  "QED" = "Drug-like", "SA" = "Drug-like", "MW" = "Drug-like", 
  "LogP" = "Drug-like", "TPSA" = "Drug-like", "HBA" = "Drug-like",

)
```

#### Validating the Disease Reversal Score

```{r}
#| label: fig-15
# read the data 
df = raw

# plot_df remove where the reversal score df full is NA
plot_df = df[!is.na(df$reversal_score_scaled)]

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = method, y = reversal_score_scaled)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.4, fill = 'lightyellow') +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = confidence, shape = significant),

  ) +

  ) +

    x = "Method",

    color = "Confidence",
    shape = "Significance"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

# calculate the network degree and netwrok distance based on the target and disease genes 
ppi_path <- "method_processing/data/full_human_ppi.rds"
ppi <- readRDS(ppi_path)
node_degrees <- igraph::degree(ppi) # degrees
# Load and Process Disease Signatures
lincs_meta <- fread("method_processing/data/LINCS/lincs_gene_meta.csv")
# Helper function to process signature files
process_lincs_signatures <- function(path) {
  data <- fread(path)
  colnames(data) <- as.character(data[1,])
  data <- data[2, 2:ncol(data)] %>% t() %>% as.data.frame()
  colnames(data) <- "z_score"
  data$pr_gene_id <- rownames(data)
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(pr_gene_id = as.character(pr_gene_id),
           z_score = as.numeric(as.character(z_score))) %>%
    inner_join(
      lincs_meta %>% mutate(pr_gene_id = as.character(pr_gene_id)), 
      by = 'pr_gene_id'
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(pr_gene_symbol, z_score) %>%
    filter(!is.na(pr_gene_symbol))
  signatures <- list(
    up = data %>% filter(z_score > 0) %>% deframe(),
    down = data %>% filter(z_score < 0) %>% deframe()
  )
  return(signatures)
}
# Load lincs1000 and smilesgen signatures
getwd()
lincs1000_1 <- process_lincs_signatures("method_processing/data/test_datasets/rest_methods/lincs1000_1.csv")
lincs1000_2 <- process_lincs_signatures("method_processing/data/test_datasets/rest_methods/lincs1000_2.csv")
glaucoma <- process_lincs_signatures("method_processing/data/test_datasets/rest_methods/glaucoma.csv")
glaucoma_bulk = process_lincs_signatures("method_processing/data/test_datasets/rest_methods/glaucoma_bulk.csv")
cardiomyopathy = process_lincs_signatures("method_processing/data/test_datasets/rest_methods/cardiomyopathy.csv")
hcc = process_lincs_signatures("method_processing/data/test_datasets/rest_methods/hcc.csv")
parkinsons = process_lincs_signatures("method_processing/data/test_datasets/rest_methods/parkinsons.csv")
# Combine up and down genes for the signature lists
disease_signatures <- list(
  lincs1000_1 = intersect(c(names(lincs1000_1$up), names(lincs1000_1$down)), V(ppi)$name),
  lincs1000_2 = intersect(c(names(lincs1000_2$up), names(lincs1000_2$down)), V(ppi)$name),
  glaucoma = intersect(c(names(glaucoma$up), names(glaucoma$down)), V(ppi)$name),
  glaucoma_bulk = intersect(c(names(glaucoma_bulk$up), names(glaucoma_bulk$down)), V(ppi)$name),
  cardiomyopathy = intersect(c(names(cardiomyopathy$up), names(cardiomyopathy$down)), V(ppi)$name),
  hcc = intersect(c(names(hcc$up), names(hcc$down)), V(ppi)$name),
  parkinsons = intersect(c(names(parkinsons$up), names(parkinsons$down)), V(ppi)$name)
)
# read the targets df

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  separate_longer_delim(Predicted_Targets, delim = ", ") %>%
  mutate(target = trimws(Predicted_Targets)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(target) & !target %in% c("None", "")) 


drug_results <- plot_df %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    drug_id = SMILES,
    score = reversal_score_scaled
  )

# processing 
mapped_drugs <- unique(as.data.frame(drug_results)[, c("drug_id", "target", "test_dataset")]) # get only unique 
mapped_drugs_long <- mapped_drugs %>%
  separate_rows(target, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
  filter(target != "" & !is.na(target)) %>%
  filter(target %in% V(ppi)$name) # separate by hgnc symbol 

drug_degrees <- mapped_drugs_long %>%
  mutate(deg = node_degrees[target]) %>%
  group_by(drug_id) %>%
  summarize(network_degree = mean(deg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") # get the mean network degree of the taget 

# compute average shortest path distance to disease genes
calculate_distance <- function(targets, test_ds) {
  if (length(targets) == 0) return(NA)
  # Determine which signature group to use based on the test_dataset
  sig_name <- case_when(
    test_ds == "glaucoma" ~ "glaucoma",
    test_ds %in% c("lincs1000_2", "lincs1000_2_m") ~ "lincs1000_2",
    test_ds %in% c("smilesgen_1", "smilesgen_1_m") ~ "smilesgen_1",
    test_ds %in% c("lincs1000_1", "lincs1000_1_m") ~ "lincs1000_1",
    TRUE ~ "lincs1000_1" # default fallback
  )
  dis_genes <- disease_signatures[[sig_name]] # get the correct signature 
  if (is.null(dis_genes) || length(dis_genes) == 0) return(NA)
  
  dists <- igraph::distances(ppi, v = targets, to = dis_genes)   # Compute shortest paths between drug targets and disease genes
  dists[is.infinite(dists)] <- NA
  mean(dists, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Calculate Drug network distance using mapped disease lists - get the drug disease and target_list in a df 
unique_drugs <- mapped_drugs_long %>%
  group_by(drug_id, test_dataset) %>%
  summarize(targets = list(target), .groups = "drop")

unique_drugs$network_distance <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(unique_drugs)), function(i) {
  calculate_distance(unique_drugs$targets[[i]], unique_drugs$test_dataset[i])
}) # applying the function here
unique_drugs_df <- as.data.frame(unique_drugs) 

drug_metrics <- unique_drugs %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(drug_id, test_dataset, network_distance) %>%
  left_join(drug_degrees, by = "drug_id") # network_degree safely maps to drug_id, Retain 'test_dataset' here so we know exactly WHICH distance belongs WHERE

# Join back to final results matching BOTH the drug and the specific context it was tested in
drug_results <- drug_results %>%
  left_join(drug_metrics, by = c("drug_id", "test_dataset"))

drug_results = drug_results %>% mutate(
  activity = case_when(action %in% c('AGONIST') ~  'Activator',
                       .default = 'Inhibitor')
)

# Now scatter plot with the x as disease reversal score and y as the network distance based on if activator or inbitor (not we consider most drugs as blockers that disrupt the protein activity or folding and not activators) and color by significance.

p1 = ggplot(drug_results, aes(x = score, y = network_distance, color = significant, shape = activity)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#ae0001", "FALSE" = "#0e1a40"),
    name = "Significant"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Disease Reversal Score",
    y = "Network Distance"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) + xlim(-2,2)


p2 = ggplot(drug_results, aes(x = significant, y = network_degree, fill = significant)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.4, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#E41A1C", "FALSE" = "#377EB8")) +
  labs(
    x = "Significant Scores",
    y = "Target Network Degree"
  ) +
```
